blocks.text: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a branch of computer science that enables machines to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence, (Figure 8.2). It allows computers to analyze data, recognize patterns, and make decisions with minimal human input. AI systems learn from experience through a process called machine learning, where algorithms are trained on large sets of data to identify trends and improve performance over time. The more data the system processes, the more accurate its results become.

AI works by combining data, algorithms, and computing power to perform intelligent tasks such as understanding speech, detecting objects in images, and predicting outcomes. It uses technologies like Neural Networks (NN) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to simulate how the human brain processes information. This allows AI to solve complex problems, automate processes, and assist in areas where traditional programming cannot handle uncertainty or vast amounts of information.
